questions.question: What is a subsequence of $(a_n)_{n\geq m}$?
options: A sequence obtained by rearranging the terms of $(a_n)$ in any order.
A sequence formed by changing the values of selected terms of $(a_n)$.
A sequence that must contain every term of $(a_n)$ exactly once.
A sequence $(a_{n_k})_{k\geq 1}$ obtained using strictly increasing indices $m\leq n_1 \lt n_2 \lt \cdots$.
questions.explanation: A subsequence selects original terms at indices $n_1<n_2<\cdots$, preserving their original order while possibly skipping indices.
questions.source_support: Definition of subsequence.

option_explanations: Arbitrary rearrangement can reverse indices and therefore need not be a subsequence.
Selected values must remain the original $a_{n_k}$ values.

A subsequence selects terms at strictly increasing indices $m\le n_1<n_2<\cdots$, so it may skip many original terms; forcing it to contain every $a_n$ exactly once describes the original sequence, not a subsequence.
